statement.p: Find a function f(x,y,z) whose level surface f=3 is the graph of the function g(x,y)= 5x+6y.

static.solution:
g(x,y)=5x+6y is the set of all points (x,y,z) satisfying z=5x+6y, or 5x+6y - z = 0. This is a level surface, but we want the surface equal to the constant value 3, not 0, so we can add 3 to both sides to get 5x+6y - z + 3 = 3. Thus, f(x,y,z) = 5x+6y-z+3 has level surface f=3 identical to the graph of g(x,y)= 5x+6y.
Of course, we could also say that the graph of g(x,y) is equivalent to z - 5x+6y = 0, so that f = z-5x-6y+3.
